q-53171.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226505/assets/db1b39e3f00fd6bb64ed738fb12213f4775d2bd7d098dfa9d0efec2192d7a64f.png)

Given that $r$, $s$ and $t$ in the above diagram are parallel, find $m∠1.$
q-53171.worked_solution:
Consider $∠2$ and $∠3$ in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226505/assets/a775b7c9ce63aa5b9f8c03fb91e7018d2f1edde5a2a2acdb099ae5ba53a874e4.png)

Note that $∠2$ and the angle whose measure is ${75}^{∘}$ are corresponding angles formed by the same transversal. Therefore, 

$$
m∠2={75}^{∘}.
$$

Similarly, note that $∠3$ and the angle whose measure is ${50}^{∘}$ are corresponding angles formed by the same transversal. Therefore, 

$$
m∠3={50}^{∘}.
$$

Let's add these measures to our diagram:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226505/assets/01462502a4fbe0b25e489cc611200beb47cd926b8a055b69b7279aa0f301850b.png)

The angles $∠1$, $∠2,$ and $∠3$ combine to give a straight angle. So, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠1+m∠2+m∠3 & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠1+{75}^{∘}+{50}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠1+{125}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠1 & ={55}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

q-117567.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226505/assets/4745f9e651eb50c345550e83ee82eb957cd28fd82e3398b667e4285bb512194c.png)

Solve for $x$ in the figure above given that $\overset{⟷}{AB}∥\overset{⟷}{CD}.$
q-117567.worked_solution:
Since the angles $∠JID$ and $∠EJB$ are corresponding angles, they are congruent and therefore have the same measure:

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠JID & =m∠EJB \\ 4x+{25}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘}-x\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have an equation that we can solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4x+{25}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘}-x \\ 5x+{25}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ 5x & ={155}^{∘} \\ \frac{5x}{5} & =\frac{{155}^{∘}}{5} \\ \frac{\cancel{5}x}{\cancel{5}} & ={31}^{∘} \\ x & ={31}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$
